answer: Sybil shear: each new identity must solve a computational puzzle whose difficulty rises with that agent’s existing reputation. An attacker’s cost grows exponentially per additional identity, since each forged node inherits a penalty multiplier from its parent in the social trellis. This forces a whisper of low-value identities to become economically absurd, as the copper needed for one hundred fakes exceeds the profit of any plausible exploit. Thus, the curve prices identity expansion as a superlinear resource, making large-scale infiltration self-defeating without any gate.
